description: Storage, 50-band. Persist a user's subjects, generated curricula/tutorials, and learning progress across three interchangeable backends — local app storage, a mounted drive, and cloud storage — so users pick what fits (privacy, portability, sync). Depends only on the shell from 10; runs in parallel with the generation bands. Anti-fabrication: each backend must actually round-trip real data (write then read back after restart); a story passes only when the selected backend genuinely persists and restores, and the gate is green.
warmup: echo 'Tauri app-data dir + fs/dialog plugins are the app-storage + mounted-drive primitives; cloud = an S3-compatible/remote config.'

userStories.title: App storage (default backend)
acceptanceCriteria: Subjects, curricula, constructed tutorials, and per-learner progress persist to the Tauri app-data directory by default, in a documented on-disk layout.
Data survives an app restart (write, restart, read back) and there is a storage abstraction the other backends plug into.
Gate green: cargo build + npm run build pass and a round-trip test passes.

userStories.title: Mounted drive and cloud backends, selectable in-app
acceptanceCriteria: The user can point storage at a mounted-drive path (via a folder picker) OR a cloud location (an S3-compatible / remote config) and select the active backend in-app.

Read/write works across the chosen backend behind the same abstraction; switching backends is handled gracefully, and unavailability (drive unplugged / cloud unreachable) surfaces a clear error rather than crashing or losing data.
Gate green: cargo build + npm run build pass and a round-trip test runs against the mounted-drive backend (cloud round-trip may use a mock/local S3); document coverage in the progress log.
